title: Administrative and Compliance Office - Crossroads Turning Points — Crossroads Turning Points Inc — 1530 West 17th Street - Pueblo County
summary: Serves as the central administrative office for Crossroads Turning Points, Inc. (CTP). Oversees the organization's operational, compliance, and privacy-related functions across all substance use and behavioral health programs. Responsibilities include: • HIPAA compliance and privacy protections • Implementation and enforcement of agency-wide policies and procedures • Management of client rights under federal confidentiality laws (HIPAA & 42 CFR Part 2) • Oversight of organizational practices and staff performance • Handling complaints related to privacy, rights, or agency operations • Coordination with program directors, quality assurance, and legal/regulatory agencies This site does not provide direct clinical services. Clients or community members may contact this office for administrative matters, privacy inquiries, records access, or concerns about agency-wide policy enforcement.

summary: The Purpose of the CSBG Program is to provide assistance to low and very low-income families and individuals in Fremont, Custer, Chaffee, and lake Counties. The program has limited funds and is not an entitlement program. CSBG funds can provide assistance with utility bills and shut off notices, medications, eviction prevention, mortgage payments, food, auto repairs (if employed), tools, & clothing for employment, home appliance repair/replacement, dental, vision and other services. To Apply:  Applications are available at location below and also available online; please bring in the additional documents required as stated on page one of the application. If you do not currently have household income you will also be required to fill out a zero income statement which is also available online. Custer County residents may apply at Custer County Department of Human Services, 205 S 6th St Westcliffe, CO 81252.

title: Developmental Screening — ECHO & Family Center Early Childhood Council — 490 North Diamond Avenue - Fremont County
summary: Provides a single point of entry into the programs coordinated by the council partnership. Offering a comprehensive developmental check-up at no cost to the family. Screening is play based and allows parents to observe and learn about their child. Parents learn if their child’s development is on track and what they can do to support their learning and growth at home. At the Screening, a child will engage in developmentally appropriate play and activities to check:   • Problem-Solving Skills   • Gross Motor Skills (crawling or running)   • Fine Motor Skills (holding a crayon, drawing)  • Independent Skills (dressing, using a spoon, etc.)   • Social-Emotional Skills  • Vision   • Hearing   • Speech and Language

title: Early Intervention Colorado — ECHO & Family Center Early Childhood Council — 490 North Diamond Avenue - Fremont County
summary: Provides support and resources to assist family members and caregivers of children with disabilities or developmental delays, from birth until a child’s 3rd birthday. Our desire is for families in our area to be linked into our network as quickly as possible. Research shows that the earlier intervention happens, the better chance a child has to overcome specific delays. These services are free and available to the general public. Once eligibility for Early Intervention is determined, a Starpoint Service Coordinator will be assigned to meet with you to create an Individualized Family Service Plan, get to know your child’s strengths and needs, and set goals to work towards. They will also support families with setting up needed supports for the child in the home or by virtual means.
